text: But this displeased Jonah greatly, and he became angry.

He prayed to the LORD, LORD, isn't this exactly what I said would happen while I was still at home? That is exactly why I hurried to run away to Tarshish in the first place — because I knew you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, overflowing with steadfast love, one who relents from sending disaster.
So now, LORD, please take my life from me, because I would rather die than go on living.
The LORD replied, Is it right for you to be this angry?
Jonah then left the city and sat down east of it. There he built himself a shelter and sat in its shade, waiting to see what would happen to the city.
Then the LORD God provided a leafy plant, and it grew up quickly over Jonah to give shade for his head and relieve his misery, and Jonah was overjoyed about the plant.
But at dawn the next day God sent a worm that attacked the plant's roots so that it withered.
Then, as the sun came up, God sent a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head until he grew faint. He wished to die, saying, Death would be better for me than this life.
But God said to Jonah, Is it right for you to be this angry about the plant? He answered, Yes, it is — angry enough to die.
The LORD said, You cared about this plant, though you did not plant it or make it grow — it sprang up in a single night and died the next.
So should I not care about Nineveh, that great city, where more than a hundred and twenty thousand people live who cannot tell their right hand from their left — not to mention all the animals?
